title: The Hardest Part Was Putting My Shoes On
scene: It's Saturday morning. The sky looks gloomy, and you're tempted to skip your walk. You promise yourself a very short outing, but it goes better than expected.
sceneJa: 土曜の朝。曇り空を見て散歩をやめようとするが、角まで行って帰ろうと決めて外に出る。歩き始めると案外気持ちよく、気づけば1時間近く経っていた。

chunks.en: I almost talked myself out of going for a walk
chunks.ja: 散歩に行くのをやめようと自分を説得しかけた

chunks.en: when I saw the gray sky.
I'd only go as far as the corner
chunks.ja: 角まで行くだけにしようと
それから引き返せばいいと
でも、いったん歩き始めると

chunks.en: I didn't feel like turning around.
chunks.ja: 引き返す気にはならなかった

chunks.en: The streets were quieter than usual,
chunks.ja: 通りはいつもより静かで

chunks.en: and the air felt surprisingly fresh.
chunks.ja: 空気も思いのほか爽やかだった

chunks.en: By the time I got home,
I'd been out for nearly an hour.
chunks.ja: 外に出てからもう1時間近く経っていた
いちばん大変だったのは
靴を履くことだったらしい

questions.question: Which chunking sounds most natural when reading the sentence aloud?
options: But once I got / going I didn't feel / like turning around
But once I got going / I didn't feel like turning around
But once / I got going I didn't / feel like turning around
questions.explanation: Keep ‘once I got going’ together: it means ‘once I started doing it’. The second chunk describes how the speaker felt after starting.

questions.question: What does ‘talked myself out of going for a walk’ mean?
options: I persuaded myself not to go for a walk.
I explained my walking plans to a friend.
I encouraged myself to walk farther.
questions.explanation: ‘Talk yourself out of doing something’ means persuade yourself not to do it. ‘Almost’ means the speaker nearly decided not to go.

questions.question: Why does the speaker say ‘the hardest part had been putting my shoes on’?
options: The shoes were too small and hurt.
The walk was difficult because the streets were crowded.
Getting started felt harder than the walk itself.
questions.explanation: The line is a playful reflection: overcoming the reluctance to start was the real challenge, not the walk.

speak: Imagine a small activity you almost skipped. Round 1: Read ‘I almost talked myself out of going for a walk / when I saw the gray sky’ slowly, pausing at the chunk boundary. Round 2: Say ‘But once I got going / I didn't feel like turning around’, stressing ‘once’ and ‘didn't’. Round 3: Read the full story with a change from reluctance to amusement. Then speak for 30 seconds: What did you almost skip? What made you start? How did you feel afterward? Use ‘I almost talked myself out of ...’ and ‘Once I got going, ...’.
review: Reuse two expressions from earlier lessons in a new context. Lesson 78: ‘I told myself ...’ (自分に言い聞かせた) was used to regain focus during table tennis; today it helps the speaker start a walk. Lesson 90: ‘By the time ...’ (〜するころには) marked a change during a football match; today it marks how much time passed on a walk. New chunks: ‘talk myself out of ...’ (自分を説得して〜をやめる), ‘once I got going’ (いったん始めると), and ‘I didn't feel like ...’ (〜する気にならなかった).
